verdict.label: HOLD / CAUTIOUS — ISM Confirms, Chip Curbs Hit NVDA, Brent Bids Back Up
verdict.rationale_short: ISM Manufacturing PMI printed at 52.7% for May — Gate 1 from the morning playbook confirmed (above 50), expansion intact. But two unforeseen developments are putting the BUY framework under pressure: the US Commerce Department closed the Malaysia AI chip loophole overnight, blocking NVDA/AMD Blackwell shipments to Chinese entities outside China; and Brent opened at $93.37 (up from Friday's $91.2) as Iran reasserts Hormuz control with the MoU still unsigned. NVDA briefly touched $217.86 (within the $213-218 add zone on COMPUTEX enthusiasm) before selling back to ~$211 on the chip-curb headline, approaching the $210 hard stop. The 30Y holds at ~4.99%, not a clean Day-2 confirmation. Stepping from BUY to HOLD: preserve optionality ahead of Friday's May payrolls and the June 17 Warsh FOMC.

bear_case: The chip-curb announcement and Brent's bid-back to $93.37 strike at the two pillars of the BUY framework simultaneously: NVDA's export-driven growth path and oil's deflationary tailwind. The Malaysia loophole closure is not a sentiment wobble — it eliminates a revenue channel that has been absorbing hundreds of thousands of Blackwell units per year, and the Commerce Department's timing (the night before COMPUTEX) signals firm enforcement intent. Brent's move from $91.2 to $93.37 on renewed Iranian Hormuz assertiveness suggests the market is beginning to price the risk that the MoU does not close, which both reverses the XLE short thesis and raises the energy-cost headwind for the broader tape. April payrolls doubled consensus (+115K vs 62-65K), suggesting May NFP on June 5 could run equally hot and hand Warsh explicit cover to signal a June 17 hike. If Brent closes above $97 and the 30Y re-breaks to 5.05% on hot June 3 data, the BUY framework requires a full Step Aside. Invalidation level: SPX closes below 7,460 with the 30Y above 5.05%, or Brent gaps above $97 on an Iran escalation — either converts the framework to Step Aside. A June 17 Warsh hike forces an exit of all longs regardless of level.
